observed: Four panels show a bell being rung, a raised bid among callers, a still phone call with the other ear covered, and a paper-plane throw toward a reaching trader.
Onlookers turn toward the bell while the bid draws nearby bodies inward.
The plane throw has an open hand and forward body weight; the receiver rises toward it.
Counter fragments, boxy monitors, phones and loose slips provide exchange context around each group.
corrections: The chest emblem is not gold; use the Atlas emblem material once picked.
No jacket colour sits near brass, which is reserved for live readings.
A paper-plane throw keeps a curled wrist so it never reads as a salute.
The shouting pose has no mouth; posture carries the mood.
Heads are a little larger than in the references so they read at 40 pixels; the exact ratio still needs a pick.
Remove decorative brass from the bell bracket and stand; this sheet does not approve a brass exception.
Keep each interaction readable without copying the overfilled panels' crowd count as a requirement.
Preserve the thrower's curled wrist and the receiver's rise together, without arrows or motion trails.

Colour audit 13 October: replace pale tiled floor with timber, strengthen the sampled monitor range (1.790:1), remove decorative brass on the bell stand, and correct gold badges, brass-like jackets, writing and gradients. Paper/floor 1.100:1 still passes the brighter-than-support rule; no extra paper contrast threshold is imposed.
